inline_comments.comment:
The alternation branches for quoted strings use capturing groups — `"([^"\\]|\\.)*"` and `'([^'\\]|\\.)*'` — which serve no purpose in a Langium terminal definition. Langium passes the full match to the value converter; capture groups are silently ignored. Use non-capturing groups `(?:...)` to avoid confusion:
```
terminal ARCH_TITLE: /\[(?:"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"|'(?:[^'\\]|\\.)*'|[\w ]+)\]/;
```

general_comments.comment: The core bug in this PR is that the value converter and the grammar regex are misaligned. The grammar regex was carefully written to support escape sequences (`\\.`) inside quoted strings, signaling that the author intended to handle embedded quotes. However, the value converter's global-replace strategy completely ignores escape sequences and unconditionally deletes every `"` and `'` character in the token. These two pieces must be brought into alignment: either the grammar should be simplified to only allow labels without embedded quote characters (and the converter's global replace is acceptable), or the converter must be fixed to properly handle quoting semantics — strip only the outer delimiters and unescape escape sequences.

The test cases under the new `describe` block each include a leading `service ... in api` or `group` declaration but none of the test inputs verify that multi-word labels with spaces (e.g. `["My API Gateway"]`) are parsed correctly. Unquoted labels already support spaces via `[\w ]+`, but it is worth confirming quoted labels work the same way. A single multi-word quoted label test would both document this behavior and guard against future regressions.
